source.title: A central alarm system that gates multi-sensory innate threat cues to the amygdala.

confidence_rationale: Direct circuit-level (optogenetic + behavioral) demonstration in mice that CGRP neurons in the external lateral parabrachial nucleus relay multi-sensory negative-valence threat signals to the central amygdala, and that this projection is required for innate threat perception and aversive memory. Maps tightly onto the upstream-broadcast-arm framing of MECH-282 (PBN-CGRP -> CeA). Confidence held below 0.9 because the paper does not isolate the specifically interoceptive (visceral malaise / hypoxia / hypoglycemia) sub-channel that MECH-282 foregrounds, and species is rodent.
failure_signatures: The paper frames CGRP threat relay as multi-sensory and innate; it does not separately validate a purely interoceptive (visceral/metabolic) input arm, so MECH-282's claim of a dissociable interoceptive channel distinct from external-threat z_harm is only partially supported here.

All causal manipulations are in mice; the broadcast-arbitration mapping onto a downstream PAG arbiter reweighted by an SD-037 override_signal is a REE-side architectural extrapolation not tested in this study.

mapping.source_claim_statement: CGRP-expressing neurons in the external lateral parabrachial nucleus (and parvocellular subparafascicular thalamus) respond to threat cues across multiple sensory modalities and relay negative valence to the central (and lateral) amygdala; both the CGRP populations and their amygdala projections are required for multi-sensory threat perception and aversive memory formation.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the empirical anchor for MECH-282's claim that a lateral-parabrachial-nucleus analog (LPB) is the upstream broadcast arm of the threat-side architecture, routing distress into harm-arbitration via PBN-CGRP -> CeA. The 'central alarm system that gates threat cues' is exactly the broadcast-into-arbitration function MECH-282 posits, parallel to the predator-side VMHdm arm.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper establishes a multi-sensory innate-threat relay, not specifically the interoceptive (visceral malaise, taste aversion, hypoxia, hypoglycemia) channel MECH-282 names as separable from external-threat z_harm. It also does not address the downstream CeA -> PAG arbiter or any override/reweighting signal; those remain REE architectural commitments, not findings transferred from this work.
mapping.source_context: Optogenetic activation/inhibition and behavioral assays (threat perception, aversive memory) in mice; cell-type-specific CGRP circuit dissection.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality cell-type-specific causal circuit study in a strong venue. Mapping fidelity strong for the broadcast-arm architecture but partial for the interoceptive-specific channel. Transfer risk moderate (rodent innate-threat circuit -> REE harm-arbitration substrate).
